claims.text: Preheating the SLM substrate and powder bed to around 500°C reduces the thermal gradient during processing.
Reduced thermal gradients from preheating minimize compositional segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating reduces residual stresses in SLM-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating reduces defect formation in SLM-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Controlled preheating can preserve a refined grain structure while reducing thermal gradients.
The proposed preheating treatment improves the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventionally fabricated counterparts.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock has a typical particle size of 10–20 μm.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder is produced by standard gas atomization.
A lower cooling rate promotes near-equilibrium solidification in this system.
Preheating enhances atomic diffusion during laser melting.
Enhanced atomic diffusion minimizes compositional segregation.
Reducing thermal gradients suppresses thermal-shock-induced defects.
Optimizing preheating duration and temperature avoids excessive grain growth.
A fine-grained microstructure is essential for improved mechanical performance in the proposed AlCrFeNiSi process.
Preheated specimens will have a more homogeneous elemental distribution than conventionally fabricated specimens.
Preheated specimens will contain fewer cracks and less porosity than conventionally fabricated specimens.
Preheating will improve the tensile strength of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventionally fabricated samples.
Preheating will improve the ductility of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventionally fabricated samples.
Conventionally fabricated or non-preheated SLM AlCrFeNiSi typically has higher residual stress, segregation, and defect density.
A preheating temperature around 500°C is within a thermal range that avoids significant grain coarsening.
